Suppose $\log(a)=m$ and $\log(b)=n$. That means $10^m=a$ and $10^n=b$.

$\begin{align}
\dfrac{\maroonE{a}}{\goldE{b}} &= \dfrac{\maroonE{10^m}}{\goldE{10^n}} &\text{Substitute.}\\\\
\dfrac{a}{b} &=10^{m-n}&\text{Quotient property}\\\\
10^{\log\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)} &=10^{m-n}&\text{Inverse relationship}\\\\
\log\left(\dfrac{a}{b}\right) &= \redE{m} - \purpleD{n}&\text{Equate the exponents.}\\\\
\log\left(\dfrac{a}{b}\right) &= \redE{\log(a)} - \purpleD{\log(b)}&\text{Substitute.}
\end{align}$
